# hrn, a small agent harness

One Go binary, `hrn`, runs tasks via the Anthropic API (`-b api`) or installed CLIs (claude, codex,
gemini, opencode, agy) and saves runs under `~/.hrn` or `$HRN_HOME`. README indexes the guides;
`docs/commands.md`, `docs/permissions.md` and `docs/run-records.md` cover commands, guards and
records. Read `PLAN.md` before taking an item; don't reopen its decisions. Older entries use `hx`
(`cmd/hx`, `$HX_HOME`); code uses `hrn`.

## Layout

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `cmd/hrn/` | The CLI and terminal renderer; batch, eval, report, prune and gc subcommands. |
| `internal/agent/` | `Backend`, `api.go`, `messages.go`, CLI adapters, instructions, prices. |
| `internal/tools/` | API tools, `guard.go`, `guardenv.go`, `secretfiles.go`, MCP bridge. |
| `internal/mcp/`, `internal/hrnmcp/` | JSON-RPC stdio and `hrn mcp` host tools. |
| `internal/batch/`, `eval/`, `report/`, `purpose/` | Worktrees, variants, tables, prompt labels. |
| `internal/runlog/`, `followup/` | Run records, pruning, continuation. |
| `internal/flow/`, `owner/`, `flowview/` | Execution events and step trees, local ownership, the shared flow view. |
| `internal/gc/`, `internal/ws/` | Merged cleanup; O_EXCL-leased slots (`.hrn/slots/<n>`). |
| `server/` | Separate module with its own `go.mod`; PostgreSQL control service and project worker. PostgreSQL tests need `HRN_TEST_DATABASE_URL`. |
| `scripts/api-check.sh` | The first real api runs. Costs real money; a maintainer runs it. |
| `.github/release.sh` | Builds the six release binaries and `SHA256SUMS` into `dist/`. |

entries.content:
## Build and test

Go 1.26.x (`go.mod`), nothing else. Before a PR, `bash scripts/check.sh` runs every CI check in
order from `.claude/skills/check/SKILL.md` (`/check` uses the same list; `--list` prints it). CI
also runs `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 40m ./...` on Linux. `-race` needs cgo: where it is
missing (a Windows PC without a C compiler), run `go test -count=3 -timeout 40m ./...` instead.
Do not attach self-hosted runners or route public contributions to private machines.
`CONTRIBUTING.md` has the CI and release details.

## Rules of this repository

- **Standard library only.** No `require` in `go.mod` and no `go.sum`. Windows syscalls use
  `syscall.NewLazyDLL`, never `golang.org/x/sys`; agent CLIs are external programs.
- **No paid model calls.** Tests use fake SSE (`internal/agent/api_test.go`) and `TestHelper*`
  processes for CLIs and MCP servers. Never read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or
  run `scripts/api-check.sh`. Run `hrn run`, `batch` or `eval` only when asked: they spend API
  credit or CLI plans, and with no `-b` a set key selects `api`.
- **Records stay loadable.** New fields in `agent.Task`, `agent.Result`, `runlog` or `batch.*` are
  additive with `omitempty`; old records on disk must still load.
- **The api history is append-only** (`api.go`): assistant turns go back exactly as received.
  Never trim, rewrite or reorder earlier messages; context is reduced server-side. With
  `mask_tool_results` set, old tool results are masked in the outgoing request only.
- **Comments say why, not what**: one line, three at most (a doc comment: one sentence, plus one
  for a non-obvious contract); no issue numbers, dates or review history. Long explanations go to
  `docs/`. `scripts/comment-check.sh` enforces it; its baseline only shrinks.
- Keep this file and `CLAUDE.md` short: the api loop loads both (`instructions.go`, 32 KiB cap).
- A release tag matches `Version` in `internal/agent/agent.go`; only a maintainer tags or releases.
- A new flag, field, command or status updates its `docs/` guide (and README if the overview
  changes). A PLAN.md item gets its box ticked, `Done: PR #n, <date>` and its deviations; an
  issue-only fix gets a Decisions-log entry naming the issue and PR. These PLAN.md changes land
  after the merge in a separate Markdown-only PR (CI skips it), never in the code PR.

entries.key: AGENTS.md > hrn, a small agent harness > Working rules
entries.content:
## Working rules

- **A branch delivers what it is for, nothing else**: one issue or PLAN.md item, a short name
  (`fix-batch-rm-deregistered`), one PR whose description lists the files it touches and why. It
  finishes everything its issue asks, with no refactors, renames or extras beyond it. Larger work
  is a feature branch: each piece's PR targets it under the rules below, and the feature branch
  reaches `main` through one PR reviewed for how the pieces fit.
- **Reviews and fixes.** Self-review with `/code-review`, then get an independent review. Every
  defect, missing test, broken house rule or security hole in what the branch touches is fixed
  before the push, blocking or not, with the smallest change; one review round's fixes go in one
  commit. Nits (wording, naming, style) are dropped, at most a line in the PR. Only a defect
  elsewhere on `main` (its own issue and branch) or a maintainer's choice becomes an issue; a
  follow-up branch files no follow-ups of its own nits.
- **Merge only what is tested.** Merge the base branch in once before the final checks and review
  (CI tests the merge with `main`), or for a conflict. Then `/check` passes, every added or changed
  behaviour has tests, CI is green on GitHub's hosted runners, the review's defects are fixed and a
  security read of the diff has nothing open, all on the head being merged. What could not be
  tested is said in the PR and waits for a maintainer. Merge through the PR only, also for
  PLAN.md's merge step: `gh pr merge <n> --merge --delete-branch --match-head-commit <sha>`. Never
  `--auto` or `--admin`, never push to `main`, never tag or release: hand over the command.
  Rulesets with no bypass protect `main` and `v*` tags; `CONTRIBUTING.md` has the details.
- **Commits**: the area first, lower case, then a plain sentence (`batch rm: name a single leftover
  file instead of counting it`), one logical change per commit. No emoji and no AI attribution
  anywhere (no `Co-Authored-By`, `Assisted-by` or "Generated with" in commits, PR text, comments
  or docs). Use the repository's git identity: check `git config user.email` first.
- Tests first, seen failing. Windows temp dirs have 8.3 short names: compare paths after
  `filepath.EvalSymlinks`. Files are LF (`.gitattributes`). Secrets are never read, printed or
  committed. Small diffs: don't restyle what you didn't change. Not sure? Ask, with one proposal.

entries.content:
# Contributing to hrn

[← README](README.md)

## Build from source

Use the Go version pinned in `go.mod` (currently 1.26.4):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/cristiangirlea/harness.git
cd harness
go build ./cmd/hrn
go test ./...
```

This produces `hrn` on Linux/macOS or `hrn.exe` on Windows. The Go code uses only the
standard library, with no third-party modules or separate runtime to install.

## Checks and pull requests

Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the complete checks, repository rules, and review/merge
requirements before changing code. Tests use fake API servers and helper processes;
do not make paid model calls as part of validation.

CI tests pull requests and pushes to `main` on standard GitHub-hosted Linux and Windows
runners. Releases build on `ubuntu-latest`. These runners are free for public repositories;
both workflows skip their jobs if the repository is private. No self-hosted runner is needed.
A change that touches only documentation Markdown (top-level `*.md` except AGENTS.md, whose script
index `scripts/verify.sh` checks; `docs/**/*.md`; `server/README.md`; `server/deploy/README.md`)
builds and tests nothing: CI's `changes` job decides, the required `test` jobs still report with
their steps skipped, and the other jobs are skipped. Any other `.md` file counts as code.
See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the security boundaries and private vulnerability reports.

- **Standard library only.** No third-party Go modules, and Windows syscalls go through
  `syscall.NewLazyDLL`, not `x/sys`. The CLI backends are external programs, not
  dependencies.
- **Tests first, seen failing.** Process-spawning code is tested by re-running the test
  binary as a helper; the API loop against a fake SSE server; MCP over in-memory pipes.
- **One pull request per increment**, small enough to review, with the plan updated in its
  own Markdown-only PR once the increment has merged.

entries.key: CONTRIBUTING.md > Contributing to hrn > Release development
entries.content:
## Release development

Releases are cut by pushing a `v*` tag that matches `agent.Version` in
`internal/agent/agent.go`: the release workflow runs the tests, builds with
`.github/release.sh`, and publishes. Tags and releases are a maintainer's to create.
A pushed `v*` tag cannot be moved or deleted (a GitHub ruleset refuses it). A tag
on the wrong commit, or a release that needs a code fix, is followed by a new
version: bump `agent.Version` and tag again. A workflow that failed for another
reason can be re-run on the same tag.
Rulesets with no bypass protect `main` and `v*` tags. GitHub refuses direct pushes
to `main`, squash or rebase merges, merges with failing or missing checks, and
moved or deleted `v*` tags. In an emergency, a maintainer turns the ruleset off
in Settings > Rules and back on afterward.

For a local release dry run, use `bash .github/release.sh`. It writes static binaries
for Linux, macOS, and Windows (amd64 and arm64), plus `SHA256SUMS`, into `dist/`.
Running that script does not publish a release. Use Git Bash on Windows.

entries.content:
## Validation notes and work queue

The original implementation notes below describe the validation still outstanding
at that stage; they are not a current compatibility matrix.

The three layers from the original brief are all here: the agent core (`hrn run`), the
orchestrator (`hrn batch`, `hrn mcp`) and the scoring layer (`hrn eval`). What remains,
in the order it is worth taking:

1. **A real run of the `api` backend**, and with it **the context-editing measurement**.
   It is the only backend that has never spoken to its API. `scripts/api-check.sh` does
   both in one command once `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set: a read-only run, a `--continue`
   of it, and one long task with context editing on and off, printed side by side with
   the server's reports of what it cleared. It makes paid API calls and records
   into a temporary `HRN_HOME`.

`PLAN.md` is the work queue and the decisions log: every increment so far, what was
deferred and why. It still calls the binary by its old name, `hx`, in entries written
before the rename.

The architecture test checks all Go imports, including tests and the server module.
Run `bash scripts/archtest-baseline.sh origin/main` to compare the baseline and
review layer map changes against the base branch; pass a different base ref when needed.

entries.content:
# hrn: run coding agents, keep every run, compare them

[![CI](https://github.com/cristiangirlea/harness/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/cristiangirlea/harness/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/cristiangirlea/harness)](https://github.com/cristiangirlea/harness/releases)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

**hrn** is one Go binary that hands a coding task to an agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini,
opencode, agy, or its own Anthropic API loop), saves everything that happened, and lets you
watch it live, replay it, run several in parallel, and score agents against each other.

![The hrn watch index: runs grouped by purpose, a running batch, and the runs list](docs/images/watch-index.png)

## How a run works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  you[You, or another agent] -->|hrn run or hrn batch| hrn[hrn]
  hrn --> backend{Backend}
  backend --> api[hrn's API loop]
  backend --> cli[Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, opencode, agy]
  hrn --> wt[Its own git worktree and branch]
  wt --> gates[Gates: your build and tests]
  gates --> record[(Run record)]
  record --> watch[hrn watch: live dashboard]
  record --> evals[hrn eval and hrn eval diff]
```

1. **You give a task.** A prompt, from the command line or a batch file.
2. **hrn picks a backend.** Its own API loop, or an agent CLI you already have installed and
   signed in to. Each uses its own plan or credentials.
3. **The agent works in its own worktree.** A batch gives each task a separate git worktree on
   its own branch, so parallel agents never step on each other.
4. **Gates check the result.** Your build and tests run after the agent finishes. A failing gate
   can trigger a retry.
5. **Everything is recorded.** Prompts, tool calls, answers, tokens, cost and timing go to a run
   record on your disk. The record stays local; the agent's own requests still go to its provider.
6. **You review and compare.** Follow a run live, replay it, merge the branches that passed, or
   run the same task set across backends and models with `hrn eval` and diff the results.

entries.content:
## Try it in a minute

You need Go 1.26.4 or later, and at least one backend. Install hrn, then see which backends
it can use:

```bash
go install github.com/cristiangirlea/harness/cmd/hrn@latest
hrn backends
```

Run a read-only task in one of your projects:

```bash
cd path/to/your/project
hrn run -b codex --mode readonly "Explain this project and its main entry points."
```

Open the dashboard in another terminal, then go to **http://127.0.0.1:8089**:

```bash
hrn watch
```

It shows runs started through hrn, as they happen. For a tour of the pages, see
[hrn watch and Ada, in pictures](docs/presentation.md).

Prefer the terminal? `hrn runs` lists recent runs, `hrn show <run-id>` replays one, and
`hrn show -f <run-id>` follows a run live.

Backend setup, with each agent's login and what it costs, is in [backends](docs/backends.md).
Updating an existing install is `hrn update`; see [hrn update](docs/commands.md#hrn-update).

entries.key: README.md > hrn: run coding agents, keep every run, compare them > What you can do
entries.content:
## What you can do

- **Run and revisit tasks.** Save prompts, tool calls, answers and usage. Continue a run on the
  same backend, or hand it to another.
- **Watch progress.** A built-in local dashboard shows runs, batches and tool calls as they happen.
- **Split work across agents.** Run a batch in separate git worktrees, with build and test gates
  and retries.
- **Compare results.** Evaluate backends and models against the same tasks and checks.
- **Connect through MCP.** Give the API loop any stdio MCP server's tools, or expose hrn itself
  as an MCP server so another agent can delegate work to it.

The Go code uses only the standard library. Agent CLIs are optional external programs: install
the ones you want.

entries.content:
## Permissions and privacy

Start with `--mode readonly` and read the [backend-specific permission
modes](docs/permissions.md#permission-modes). The command guard is a guardrail, not an
operating-system sandbox, and the same mode does not mean identical permissions on every backend.

Run records can contain source code, prompts and tool output, so treat the records folder as
you would the code itself. The dashboard listens on loopback by default. `--lan` lets anyone on
the selected network read the records without a login. With `--public`, the page is reachable
beyond loopback only through a Cloudflare Tunnel and Access application that you set up; see
[watch exposure](docs/watch.md#behind-cloudflare-access). Security boundaries and how to report a
vulnerability are in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

entries.key: server/README.md > PostgreSQL control service and project worker
entries.content:
# PostgreSQL control service and project worker

`server/` is a separate Go module. The root `hrn` CLI remains standalone and
standard library only. This module uses pgx to keep tenants, projects, jobs,
ownership, events, and durable API checkpoints in PostgreSQL. The control
service accepts jobs over HTTP; a project worker claims and heartbeats them,
runs jobs through the hrn binary, and saves checkpoints. An accepted job
survives the submitting client's disconnect and a control service restart. Recovery after
worker loss requires operator confirmation that the old executor stopped.

The worker is a development fixture: it accepts only read-only API jobs with
a positive cost ceiling, uses a loopback fake model, and has no tools, shell,
or external agent CLI execution. It does not fetch the registered repository
or provide an isolation boundary. Its workspace manifests detect identity drift; they do
not make filesystem changes and database checkpoints atomic.

Both submission and the durable API run path refuse MCP servers and
`allow_dangerous`. A stored job that bypassed submission with either option
finishes as `failed`, with the refusal in its result, before any model call.

entries.key: server/README.md > PostgreSQL control service and project worker > Local checks
entries.content:
## Local checks

Run from `server/`:

```text
go vet ./...
go build ./...
go test -count=1 ./...
```

PostgreSQL tests skip unless `HRN_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set. For a disposable
fixture, start PostgreSQL using `compose.dev.yaml` from the repository root:

```text
docker compose -f server/compose.dev.yaml up -d
```

Then set `HRN_TEST_DATABASE_URL` to
`postgres://postgres:fixture-only@127.0.0.1:54329/harness_test?sslmode=disable`
and run `go test -count=1 ./...` in `server/`. Tests create and remove their own
schemas. Stop the fixture with `docker compose -f server/compose.dev.yaml down`.

Regenerate the knowledge goldens with `HRN_UPDATE_WIRE_FIXTURES=1`, and the
client recording with `HRN_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1` and `HRN_TEST_DATABASE_URL` set.
Copy `server/platform/testdata/knowledge` to `internal/retrieval/testdata/wire`
and `server/platform/testdata/remote` to `internal/remote/testdata/server`; the
fixture identity test fails until the copies match.

For a private local control service, set `HRN_DATABASE_URL` and distinct random
`HRN_OPERATOR_TOKEN` and `HRN_SCALER_TOKEN` values of at least 32 characters.
`hrn-server` also accepts `HRN_DATABASE_URL_FILE`, `HRN_OPERATOR_TOKEN_FILE`,
and `HRN_SCALER_TOKEN_FILE`; `hrn-worker` accepts `HRN_WORKER_TOKEN_FILE`.
Each `_FILE` variable names a regular file of at most 64 KiB instead of a
non-empty direct value; exactly one trailing LF or CRLF is removed, and an
empty result is rejected.
Run `go run ./cmd/hrn-server migrate`, then `go run ./cmd/hrn-server serve`
from `server/`. The default `HRN_LISTEN` address is `127.0.0.1:8088`.
Without TLS, only loopback IP literals (`127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`, for example
`[::1]:8088`) are allowed. Host names (including `localhost`), empty hosts
such as `:8088`, and non-loopback addresses require both `HRN_TLS_CERT_FILE`
and `HRN_TLS_KEY_FILE`; otherwise startup is refused before listening. Run
`go run ./cmd/hrn-fixture-model` for the local model and configure the worker
with `HRN_CONTROL_URL`, `HRN_FIXTURE_API_URL`, `HRN_PROJECT_ID`,
`HRN_WORKER_TOKEN`, and an existing absolute `HRN_WORKSPACE_ROOT`. The worker
command is `go run ./cmd/hrn-worker`.
The worker requires the `hrn` binary to run jobs and checks `hrn version` at
startup, with a 10-second timeout. Set
`HRN_WORKER_HRN` or pass `-hrn` to select the binary; the flag takes precedence.
The default is `hrn` on PATH. The container image supplies the binary and sets
`HRN_WORKER_HRN` to its absolute path.

Tenant budgets and spending reservation are not enforced yet (still open in
the durable workers spec): any tenant can queue any number of jobs, each up to
its own `max_cost_usd`. Set `HRN_MAX_COST_USD_PER_JOB` (a positive number of
USD) to cap that ceiling: a submission above it is refused with 422
`cost_limit` naming the limit, and an invalid value stops startup. Unset means
no server cap. Clients can add their own with `HRN_REMOTE_MAX_COST_USD`.

entries.content:
## Job events

`GET /v1/jobs/{job}/events?tenant_id=...&project_id=...` requires the tenant's
bearer token. By default it returns a JSON page of up to 100 events. Set
`Accept: text/event-stream` to receive the backlog and then live events, polled
once per second. Resume after the last received event ID using `after` or
`Last-Event-ID`; if both are supplied they must match. A job's event IDs
become visible in increasing order, because each event is written while its job's
row is locked, so a cursor never skips an event that commits later.

Each control service instance allows at most four open SSE streams per tenant,
shared across its projects and jobs. Further streams receive HTTP 429 with a
JSON `stream_limit` error. A slot is released whenever its stream ends, including
client disconnects. JSON event requests do not consume stream slots.

A stream drains the backlog and closes when the job is `succeeded`, `failed`,
or `canceled`, including when it receives that terminal event live. An already
terminal job with no events after the cursor closes immediately. States such as
`waiting_approval` and `recovery_required` remain live. Streams also close after
30 minutes; reconnect with the last received cursor to continue without replaying
earlier events.

entries.key: server/README.md > PostgreSQL control service and project worker > Schema and recovery
entries.content:
## Schema and recovery

Migration 001 creates the control schema. Migration 002 snapshots the project
repository URL when a job is accepted. It refuses to upgrade a schema 1
database that contains jobs, because their accepted URLs cannot be recovered
safely. Migration 003 adds scoped, immutable project knowledge and retrieval
records. The integration tests cover both refusal and the empty schema upgrade.
Opening an older schema requests the explicit `migrate` command; startup never
migrates it automatically.
The worker uses version 2 workspace manifests and refuses older or mismatched
manifests. An uncertain operation enters `recovery_required` instead of being
silently replayed. The control service does not independently verify that an
old worker or node has stopped.

The checkpoint store is a trust boundary: it must commit before acknowledging a
save, fence stale owners, and preserve immutable versions. The API checkpoint's
task digest binds task settings, not the stored `Result.CostUSD`, `Started`, or
`Deadline`. Recovery trusts those values from the store; changing them can reset
spent budget or the clock. Keep checkpoint write access and store credentials
outside execution tools and untrusted workspace/model content.

The cost ceiling prevents the next model request. Tools from an already paid,
checkpointed response still run on recovery even if that response reached the
ceiling; their committed outcomes are not repeated. The original deadline still
applies. Cancellation or timeout between committed operations reports `canceled`
or `timeout` without `recovery_required`. A definite non-retryable HTTP 4xx is
an error without recovery; a context-management 400 retries without that feature
after saving a new model intent. Interrupted requests, retryable HTTP errors,
and failed checkpoint saves remain uncertain and require recovery.

entries.content:
## Approved project knowledge

Only the control service connects to PostgreSQL. Operators import reviewed
source material with `HRN_OPERATOR_TOKEN`; model-generated candidates are
rejected. Read clients use `HRN_SERVER_URL`, `HRN_TENANT_TOKEN` (or the exact
project's worker token), and optionally `HRN_SERVER_CA_FILE`. Knowledge
commands use `HRN_OPERATOR_TOKEN` for mutations and never fall back to the
read credential. Credentials stay outside request files and packets.
Operator review is the control: the import deny list screens every text field
but catches obvious mistakes only, including private credential paths, key
headers, common token shapes, and a few instruction-injection phrases.
The `.env` path check matches whole segments (split on `/`, whitespace, quotes,
`=`, `,` and `;`) and `.env.<suffix>` files; `.envrc` and `docs/.environment.md`
are allowed. Path checks apply to paths, keys and identifiers, not to the prose
of `content`, `evidence` and `review_evidence`, so a note such as "copy
.env.example to .env" imports; key headers and token shapes are refused in every field.
Import refusals name the field and deny-list pattern that matched, without
including the submitted text.

The API uses these scoped JSON operations:

| Route | Operation | Credential |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/knowledge/import` | Import a reviewed, immutable version | Operator |
| `POST /v1/knowledge/change` | Activate, disable, or roll back a version | Operator |
| `POST /v1/knowledge/admission` | Record a verdict; activate an admitted candidate while its baseline stays active | Operator |
| `POST /v1/knowledge/search` | Return an audited, bounded packet | Tenant, project worker, or operator |
| `POST /v1/knowledge/inspect` | Inspect a version | Tenant, project worker, or operator |
| `POST /v1/knowledge/active` | Read active and previous pointers | Tenant, project worker, or operator |

A reviewed import request in `seed.json` has this shape:

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t_<32 hex>", "project_id": "p_<32 hex>",
  "backend": "codex", "model": "<configured model>",
  "revision": "<full reviewed commit SHA>",
  "origin": "reviewed_source", "reviewed_by": "<reviewer>",
  "review_evidence": "<source review reference>",
  "entries": [{
    "key": "build-guide", "content": "<reviewed project guidance>",
    "source": "docs/build.md", "evidence": "<verification reference>",
    "identifiers": ["BuildProject", "src/build.go"]
  }]
}
```

```text
hrn knowledge import seed.json
hrn knowledge active scope.json
hrn knowledge activate change.json
hrn knowledge search search.json
hrn knowledge inspect inspect.json
hrn knowledge disable change.json
hrn knowledge rollback change.json
```

`scope.json` contains tenant_id/project_id/backend/model/revision. `change.json`
adds version_id for activate and expected_generation from `active`; disable and
rollback need scope and expected_generation. `search.json` adds query and
optionally version_id; `inspect.json` adds version_id. Inputs reject unknown
fields, including credential fields. Search matches exact scope and ranks
identifiers, paths, and errors before `simple` text matches, with stable ties.
Search materializes the version's members before matching their entries.
Identifiers may include spaces for multi-word errors. Exact query candidates
also omit trailing sentence periods and colons, preserving internal path punctuation.
Joined candidates contain at most 8 words; each search sends at most 256 exact
candidates, each limited to 256 bytes.
The optional search `attempt` must be between 0 and 2147483647 inclusive.
An empty or no-match packet is valid; packets contain at most 8192 bytes of
reference text and an audit ID.

entries.content:
## hrn feed

`hrn feed` requires `-b BACKEND` and exactly one of `--task TEXT` or
`--task-file PATH`. Each item receives that instruction. `--model NAME` selects
the model. `--in PATH` selects JSONL input; omitted, empty or `-` reads stdin.
`--out PATH` writes JSONL results; omitted writes stdout. Input and output must
be different files. `--parallel N` defaults to 4 and accepts 1 through 16.
`--timeout D` is a positive per-item deadline, default 2m. `--max-tokens N`
sets an output token ceiling from 1 through 64000 on `api`; other backends
reject it. A response cut at this ceiling returns `status: error` with
`error: "response hit max_tokens"` and no output.

`--thinking off|on` defaults to `off` and affects only `api`; CLI backends
ignore it. Off omits `thinking` and sends llama.cpp's
`chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` only to loopback HTTP
endpoints; on preserves adaptive thinking. In a local llama.cpp measurement
with Gemma 4 26B-A4B, disabling thinking reduced a one-word answer from 160-200
output tokens and 6.8 s to 2 tokens and 1.1 s, with the same answer.

Input is one JSON object with required string `text` and optional string `id`,
or a bare JSON string, per line. Missing IDs use the one-based line number.
Empty strings are valid. Invalid JSON, missing or non-string text, non-string
IDs and lines over 64 KiB produce `invalid` results and processing continues.
The limit counts bytes before LF, including a CR if present.

Each result contains `id`, `status` (`ok`, `error`, `invalid`, `timeout`),
`output`, `run_id`, `duration_ms`, `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`, plus
`error` on failure. Invalid lines have no run ID and zero counters. Lines are
flushed as items finish, so their order can differ from the input. A final stderr
line reports items, ok, failed, wall time and items per second. Per-item failures
are reported in JSONL; command setup, input/output failures and cancellation
return a nonzero exit code.

Items run in one empty temporary workspace per feed, removed at the end, with
mode `readonly`, `max_turns: 1` and purpose `none`. API runs have no tools or
project instructions. Claude runs are lean with all built-in tools disabled
(`--tools ""`) and strict MCP configuration with no servers. Other CLI backends
are refused because they cannot run without tools yet. No implicit backend,
purpose routing, MCP configuration or usage-limit switching is used.
Ctrl-C stops starting items and lets those running finish up to their deadlines.
For the local API restriction and pipeline design, see [Text feeds](feed.md).

entries.content:
## Automatic gc

Automatic cleanup is off by default. To enable it, create `$HRN_HOME/gc.json` (or
`~/.hrn/gc.json` when `HRN_HOME` is unset), for example:

```json
{"enabled": true, "roots": ["E:\\work"], "interval": "24h", "free_below_bytes": 53687091200}
```

Roots must be existing absolute directories below a filesystem root and are never discovered automatically. With no PATH arguments,
`hrn gc` uses these roots when present; otherwise it uses the current directory. Explicit
PATH arguments override them. Set `enabled` to false or remove the file to turn automatic
cleanup off. `interval` defaults to 24h and accepts a positive Go duration; the free-space
target defaults to 50 GiB and is expressed in bytes. Zero selects the default.

While `hrn watch` runs, it checks once a minute and starts a pass when due, including at
startup. It applies the ordinary worktree and cache rules with a one-hour merge grace,
24-hour idle threshold, two-hour minimum idle and the configured free-space target; slot
caches are trimmed under the usual rules. This does not guarantee a target when eligible
space is insufficient. A successful `hrn batch merge` also checks that repository's
batch-owned worktrees against the same proof of landing, without running the cache pass.

Manual apply and automatic passes share `$HRN_HOME/gc.lock` and never overlap. A dead
holder or lock older than six hours is taken over only after the OS lock is available;
takeovers are logged. A lock held beyond the configured interval appears in watch and on
stderr. `$HRN_HOME/gc.log` holds
JSON lines with timestamps, paths, estimated bytes, reasons and outcomes; older entries are
discarded to keep it under 1 MiB. A started entry records planned actions before removal;
without a completed entry the outcome is uncertain. Errors appear in the log and watch's
local index (and on watch's stderr); refresh the page to see the latest pass.
`$HRN_HOME/gc-last` retains the last scheduled start independently of log rotation.

For `--continue ID`, `--fresh` starts a bounded hand-over and `--resume` uses the saved session. A codex run continued on codex defaults to fresh; MCP and exec callers use explicit `fresh: false` to resume. See [Continuing a run](backends.md#continuing-a-run).

`--lean=false` (claude and codex are lean by default: only the run's `--mcp` servers, and on
claude no skills; false loads everything), `--skills` (claude: keep skills and slash commands in
a lean run; see [What a run loads](backends.md#what-a-run-loads);
codex, gemini, opencode and agy report `skills: not enforced`),
`--compact-window N` (claude: compact at N tokens, 100000 to 1000000, or `auto`; see
[Compaction window](backends.md#compaction-window)),
`--append-system-prompt TEXT` (api and claude: added after the backend's own system prompt,
at most 16 KiB), `--no-skills` (claude: skills off; see
[Harness variants](evaluations.md#harness-variants)),
`--allow-dangerous`, `--inherit-env` (CLI backends: your whole environment; see
[A clean environment for CLI workers](backends.md#a-clean-environment-for-cli-workers)),
`--no-switch` (see
[When a plan's usage limit is reached](backends.md#when-a-plans-usage-limit-is-reached)),
`--issue REF` (the GitHub issue the run works on: `owner/name#N`, its URL, or `#N` for the
workspace's origin; leased before the agent starts, so a second run for it exits 2 naming the
holder) and `--take-over` (take that lease from its holder; see
[Issue leases](workspaces.md#issue-leases)), and the budgets below.
For claude runs whose resolved purpose is `review` or `test`, an unset `--max-turns`
defaults to 30 and is saved in the run record. An explicit positive value overrides it;
a negative value leaves claude without a turn limit. Zero is treated as unset. The
api default remains 50 turns.
`--shape-tools` opts the api backend into summaries of large terminal, log and
test-runner results from shell and MCP tools, with the full original saved behind
a handle (see [Run records](run-records.md#run-records)). It is off by default
pending the #296 eval; JSON and tabular summaries are deferred. Summaries must
preserve failing tests and error lines and introduce no numbers, negations or
paths absent from the original; a rejected summary uses the existing cut. This
includes generated counts, so a count absent from the original also rejects the
summary. Failing-test diagnostics must stay with their test name, in order;
ambiguous interleaved diagnostics reject the summary and use the existing cut.
Sequential subtests are nested, not interleaved: a diagnostic after `=== RUN TestA/sub`
belongs to that subtest while its parent waits. Go before 1.20 prints no `=== NAME`
marker when the parent logs again after a subtest, so that parent diagnostic is kept with the
subtest; if the subtest passed, the summary drops it and only `read_original` shows it.
`--shape-tools=false` keeps the existing behavior. The additive `shape_tools`
boolean is also available in run options, batch specs/tasks and MCP
run inputs. Eval matrix variants each select `shape_tools` (default false),
overriding task/spec shaping so a suite can compare raw and shaped variants;
give the variants distinct names. This flag does not change CLI backend tools.
`--parse-check` opts the api backend's `edit_file` and `write_file` tools into
syntax checks for `.go` and `.json` files (case-insensitive). It is off by default;
`parse_check` is also available in run options, batch specs/tasks and MCP run
inputs. Invalid changes are refused with a line and column, leaving the file
unchanged. Existing unparseable files remain editable so they can be repaired;
new files are checked. Make each edit whole. Shell, MCP and CLI tools are unaffected.

`--retrieval off|optional|required` opts into project references; enabled modes
require `--retrieval-tenant`, `--retrieval-project`, `--retrieval-revision` and
an explicit `--model`. `--retrieval-version` pins a version; otherwise the
active version is resolved once and saved with the run. A pin stays with its
backend: `--continue` with `--retrieval optional|required` on another backend than
the chain's latest pin is refused with exit 2 before anything runs, naming the
pinned run and its version. Continue on the pin's backend, start a fresh run, or
continue with retrieval off to hand the transcript over (see
[Continuing a run](backends.md#continuing-a-run)).

entries.content:
### Declared purpose

`hrn run --purpose CATEGORY` declares what a run is for: `review`, `debug`,
`implement`, `refactor`, `test`, `research`, `plan` or `ops`. An invalid flag value
is refused with exit 2 before the run starts. The MCP `run` tool takes the same
optional `purpose` string, and each task in a CLI or MCP batch spec may set it;
invalid values are refused before any task runs. Flag and MCP/batch field values
are case-sensitive and must use the lowercase spellings above (`Review` is refused).

Without an explicit value, a `Purpose: <category>` header on the prompt's first
non-blank line supplies the declaration. The header label and category are
case-insensitive; a non-category value, including free text or `unknown`, is
ignored as a declaration and is never an error; that header line is also excluded
from keyword classification. The explicit value takes
precedence over the header. The effective declaration is saved in `task.purpose`;
no prompt text is added, removed or changed. Watch and reports use it before
falling back to the keyword classifier. An invalid stored `task.purpose` is ignored,
falling back to a valid header or the classifier.

The classifier reads only the lead of a prompt, because long briefs mention every
keyword ("review the diff", "CI", "deploy") somewhere later: the first non-blank
paragraph, and the second only when no rule matches the first, each lowercased and
capped at 600 bytes. An instruction after leading labels such as `Repository: hrn`
is tried before the paragraph as written, and hand-over headings such as
`## Hand-over` are skipped. Its CI, deploy and compare keywords count only in the
lead's first sentence and never inside a branch, file or path name (`ci/pin`,
`deploy-x`, `ci.yml`).

A continued run (`hrn run --continue`, or the MCP `run` tool with `continue_run_id`)
keeps the earlier run's purpose when neither `--purpose`/`purpose` nor a
header names one, as it keeps the mode: its declared purpose, or else the category
the classifier gave its prompt (nothing when that was `unknown`), saved in
`task.purpose` like a declaration. A short follow-up such as "now fix what you
found" is therefore not re-classified. `hrn exec` takes the same optional `purpose`
on `start` (see [the exec protocol](exec-protocol.md#start-caller-exactly-one-the-first-line)).
A batch task's declared purpose shows in `hrn batch show`'s table, the MCP
`batch_show` text and the task list on the watch batch page.

entries.content:
### hrn exec

`hrn exec --protocol v1` lets a supervising program start, follow, cancel and record
one run per process without parsing terminal output. stdin and stdout carry JSON
lines: hrn sends `hello` first, then accepts one `start`, streams complete events,
and ends with `result`. Closing stdin or interrupting hrn cancels the run. See
[the v1 protocol](exec-protocol.md) for messages, capabilities, limits and exit codes.

### hrn update

`hrn update` moves every hrn on this computer to another build in one step, the routine
that used to be done by hand after a merge.

**Sources.** Without a flag it takes the newest GitHub release of `cristiangirlea/harness`:
the asset for this platform (`hrn_<version>_<os>_<arch>[.exe]`, as `.github/release.sh`
names them) and `SHA256SUMS`, and refuses to go on when the checksum does not match. A
`GITHUB_TOKEN` in the environment is sent to the API when present and never printed.
`--ref REF` runs `go install github.com/cristiangirlea/harness/cmd/hrn@REF` into a temporary
`GOBIN` (with `GOFLAGS` unset and `GOPROXY` as configured); `--main` is `--ref main`; both
need Go on `PATH` and say so otherwise. `--file PATH` takes a binary already built, say the
one a session built in a scratch folder. Whatever the source, the candidate is run once with
`version` and nothing else, after the checksum. The command prints `installed:` and
`candidate:` lines and stops with `already current` when every target names the same commit or
module version as the candidate; otherwise a target that already does is listed as `already
current` and left alone (no backup, its watch not restarted), and the others are updated.
Two `modified` builds of one commit count as the same only when their files contain identical bytes.

**Targets.** The running executable (resolved through symlinks) and every `hrn` (`hrn.exe`) on
`PATH`, in `$GOPATH/bin` or `~/go/bin` and, on Windows, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hrn`, each listed
once with its version line. A file called hrn that does not answer `version` like hrn is left
alone.

**Backups.** Each target is renamed to `hrn-<build>-<yyyymmdd-hhmm>.prev[.exe]` beside it
(`<build>` is its short commit or module version, else `unknown`): Windows refuses to overwrite
a running binary but allows the rename. The candidate is copied in under the original name
with mode 0755 and run with `version`; when that fails or says something else, the backup goes
back and the target is reported as failed. The others are still done, and the exit code is 1
when any failed. `--dry-run` prints the plan and changes nothing.

**Rollback.** `hrn update --rollback` finds the newest `hrn-*.prev` beside each target and swaps
it back the same way, the current binary becoming `hrn-<build>-<stamp>.rolledback[.exe]`. A
target without a backup is reported as failed.

**The watch.** A running `hrn watch` started from one of the targets is stopped after the swap
and the new binary started detached with the same arguments, so `--lan`, `--addr` and
`--public` settings survive. Its output goes to the files the old one wrote to where the
system can tell (Linux), else to `watch-<port>.log` under `HRN_HOME`. The command prints
`watch restarted on <addr>` with the new pid. A watch whose binary could not be replaced is
left running. On macOS the watch is found through `ps`, which shows the program as it was typed;
a bare `hrn` is looked up on the `PATH` of `hrn update` itself.

**MCP servers.** Running `hrn mcp` processes are listed under "still on the old build until their
host restarts them", with pid, parent and start time, and never stopped: the host (Claude Code,
Codex) that started them owns them and respawns them on its next start.

entries.content:
### Remote development jobs

Set `HRN_SERVER_URL` to the control service HTTPS origin, `HRN_TENANT_TOKEN` to an
issued tenant token, and optionally `HRN_SERVER_CA_FILE` to a PEM CA file. HTTP
is accepted only for loopback fixtures. The tenant and project IDs are issued
by the server; `--base-ref` is a full Git commit registered for the project.
The origin may have a trailing `/`, but no credentials, other path, query
(including an empty `?`), or fragment, and its hostname may not be empty. The CA
path must name a regular file of at most 1 MiB; symlinks to regular files are
accepted. Devices, FIFOs and pipes are refused before they are opened, and on
Windows so are `\\.\`, `\\?\` and `\??\` paths and reserved device names such as
`NUL` or `COM1`.
Submission requires a stable idempotency key and a positive USD cost ceiling.
When `HRN_REMOTE_MAX_COST_USD` is set, a `--max-cost` above it is refused before
any request; unset means no client cap. The control service does not reserve
tenant budgets yet, so this and the server's `HRN_MAX_COST_USD_PER_JOB` (see
[server/README.md](../server/README.md)) are the spending control.
The prompt can be supplied as arguments or on stdin. Remote jobs currently
support only the read-only `api` backend. See [MCP](mcp.md#hrn-as-an-mcp-server)
for the corresponding tools.
Remote jobs refuse enabled retrieval options until the worker can honor their
version pin; use a local run for opted-in retrieval.
MCP servers and `allow_dangerous` are refused at submission and again by the
durable API run path; a stored job with either option fails with a clear result
error before any model call.

`hrn remote events --watch` prints events until it prints one that ends the job,
then exits with status 0, including when the job failed or was canceled. Terminal
event kinds are `succeeded`, `failed`, and `canceled`; `admission_timeout` and
`recovery_resolved` also end the watch when their `details.state` is terminal.
The watch reconnects from the last printed event ID if a stream ends before a
terminal event. Before streaming it reads the job's state (the request `hrn remote
show` makes): if the job has already ended, it prints the events after `--after`, if
any, and exits with status 0 without waiting. Ctrl-C ends the watch early.
Each event's data must be JSON of at most 1 MiB in total, however many `data:`
lines carry it; the space after a field's colon is optional. C1 control
characters (U+0080 to U+009F) and invalid UTF-8 are printed as `\u` escapes, so
the terminal never reads them as control sequences.

entries.content:
### Project knowledge

`hrn knowledge markdown -request base.json FILE...` reads only the named files,
resolved inside the repository root with files under `.git` refused, and writes
JSON only. The base import must
have no entries and a non-empty revision; its other fields are kept. Heading
sections merge below `-min-words` (100), split above `-max-words` (800) or 16384
bytes, and overlap by `-overlap-words` (40) when split. Keys carry the relative
path and heading ancestry, sources carry `path@revision`, and evidence records
the limits. Review the resulting entries and import as before. Entry keys weigh
more than content in ranking (`simple-or-exact-v3`), and a long entry that does
not fit the 8 KiB packet arrives as an excerpt marked `excerpt=true`; its
`content` contains the excerpt and `excerpt` is omitted for whole entries.
Imports refuse entries marked as excerpts.

`hrn knowledge import|search|inspect|active|activate|disable|rollback request.json`
accepts one JSON request file and prints a JSON response. `import`, `activate`,
`disable`, and `rollback` require `HRN_OPERATOR_TOKEN`; read commands use
`HRN_TENANT_TOKEN` or the exact project's worker credential. Set
`HRN_SERVER_URL` and optionally `HRN_SERVER_CA_FILE` for the control service.
Credentials are never placed in request files.

`hrn knowledge admit --version ID --spec FILE -b claude|codex` compares the
active version and candidate on the same held-out tasks, using the spec's repeats
(at least two). `--held-out` defaults to 0.3; `--seed` defaults to zero. The spec
must select required retrieval and one tenant, project, revision and model for
all tasks. Both `HRN_OPERATOR_TOKEN` and `HRN_TENANT_TOKEN` are needed: the
operator records the verdict and the tenant credential retrieves context during
the eval. Source run IDs are extracted from entry evidence or supplied with
repeatable `--source-run`; at least one is required. The command prints one JSON
admission record. Higher pass rate beyond repeat movement, or equal pass rate
with at least 10% fewer passing median tokens and settled variance, admits the
candidate. Inconclusive comparisons stay pending; failed-attempt tokens are
reported separately. The previous active version remains available for rollback.

An operator imports only reviewed sources with `origin: "reviewed_source"`,
`reviewed_by`, and `review_evidence`; model-generated candidates are rejected.
Each request names the exact tenant, project, backend, model, and full Git
revision. Imported content revisions and their version membership are
immutable. `active` returns the active and previous version pointers and their
generation. `activate`, `disable`, and `rollback` use `expected_generation` to
reject concurrent changes. `search` uses `query` and optionally `version_id`;
it returns an audited packet capped at 8192 bytes, including a valid empty or
no-match result. `inspect` reads a `version_id`. The server records each search
and ties its query and packet digests to the exact UTF-8 bytes. See
[the control service guide](../server/README.md#approved-project-knowledge) for
the protocol table and request examples.

entries.key: docs/commands.md > Command reference > Automatic gc > Budgets
entries.content:
### Budgets

Turns are a poor proxy for what a run costs: most of the spend is the context
re-sent every turn. Three ceilings, all optional and all off by default.

| Flag | Spec / MCP field | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--timeout 20m` | `timeout` | Ends the run when the deadline passes, on every backend. The result is `timeout`, not `canceled`, so a slow run is distinguishable from an interrupted one. |
| `--max-cost 2.50` | `max_cost_usd` | The api loop stops before a turn that would take its estimated cost past the limit. The result is `budget`, and the cost so far is still recorded. |
| `--task-budget 64000` | `task_budget` | Tells the api backend's model how many tokens it has for the whole task, so it paces itself and finishes rather than being cut off. Minimum 20000, checked before the run starts. |
| `--mask-tool-results N` | `mask_tool_results` | Opt into masking older tool results in outgoing api requests, in steps of N, keeping the newest N to 2N-1 whole once masking starts. Replaces server clearing; stored history stays whole. Default 0 (off); negative values are rejected. See [backends](backends.md#context-management). |

The CLI backends cannot enforce a cost or token ceiling, so they say so once and
carry on; the timeout applies to them all the same. The cost ceiling is checked against
hrn's own estimate, so a model with no price in the table cannot be capped and the run
says so instead of pretending.

Agent CLIs and shell commands start in a Windows Job Object or a Unix process group.
Cancel or timeout kills that tree; CLI cleanup can take up to about 15 seconds while
stdout/stderr reads are bounded and remaining processes are checked (survivors or
unavailable Windows containment are reported). On Windows, a CLI's leftover background
processes end when the run ends, including after a normal exit, because the job is
closed. On Unix, background processes survive a normal exit and are killed only on
cancel or timeout; children can escape the group with setsid.

On Unix, Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and SIGHUP cancel runs. A process in the tree that reads the
terminal (such as a credential or host-key prompt) stops because the tree is not the
terminal's foreground process group.

On Windows, closing the console, logging off or shutting down reaches hrn as
SIGTERM. It has a few seconds to save the cancelled record while the job ends the
process tree. On Linux with procfs mounted with hidepid=2, a tree member owned by
another user (sudo or a setuid helper) is invisible to the check, so "gone" can be
optimistic.

Where a cost comes from depends on the backend. The claude and opencode CLIs report one
themselves; on a subscription that figure is what the run would cost at API list
prices, not a charge. codex, gemini and agy report none. The API returns token counts only,
so the api backend prices them from a table in `internal/agent/api.go`: Anthropic's
first-party list prices per model, including the newer models' own cache-read prices,
with cache writes at 1.25x input. A dated snapshot id such as
`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` is priced as its model. A model missing from the table has
no estimate, and the run says so at the start rather than showing a cost of zero.

entries.content:
### Practice

`hrn bot practice` shows today's UTC exercise. `swap` selects another before it is
answered; `answer` reads stdin, or `answer --file PATH` reads a file, saves it and
shows the reveal. `mark got_it`, `mark partly`, or `mark missed` records a self-mark.
`read owner/repo#n` starts a read of an open pull request; answer and mark it the
same way. Return to the daily exercise with `hrn bot practice`. Up to three reads
may be started per UTC day, including a daily exercise of that kind. The read earns
experience only if the pull request merges after the answer. GitHub exercises need
`gh`; recall reads the committed `PLAN.md` from repositories in run and batch records.
Material and reveals are masked before storage. Practice remains available when the
game is disabled.

entries.content:
## Batches

`hrn batch tasks.json` runs every task in the file against one repository, `parallel`
agents at a time, each in its own git worktree on its own branch. After an agent
finishes, the gate commands run in that worktree; a task whose run or gates fail is
retried on the next backend in `retry`. Every attempt is an ordinary recorded run.

```json
{
  "parallel": 3,
  "backend": "claude",
  "mode": "yolo",
  "gate": ["go build ./...", "go test ./..."],
  "retry": ["opencode"],
  "tasks": [
    {"id": "fix-add", "prompt": "add() in math.go subtracts. Fix it and add a test."},
    {"prompt": "Make list_files skip .venv directories.", "backend": "api", "gate": ["go test ./internal/tools"]}
  ]
}
```

`dir` (default: the file's directory) is any path inside the repository. Task fields
override the file's defaults of the same name; `id` defaults to `t1`, `t2`, …. A task's
`"gate": []` is refused: leave `gate` out to use the spec's gates, or move the gates onto
the tasks that need them (an answer-only task then has none), so a record reads as the run ran.

Every shared run option (`agent.Options`) is a spec field under the same name with
underscores (`--max-turns` is `max_turns`, `--max-cost` is `max_cost_usd`), on the spec
or on a task; the MCP `run` tool takes the same names. They are one struct in the code
(`agent.Options`), so the three cannot drift apart. A task's value replaces the spec's;
a switch a task turns on stays on, except `lean` and `skills`: lean is on by default for
tasks on claude and codex and a task can set it to `false` (see
[What a run loads](backends.md#what-a-run-loads)); a task's own `mcp` list replaces the spec's, and an
empty list (`"mcp": []`) means no servers at all, not even `~/.hrn/mcp.json`. Every list
is checked before the first task starts.

`issue` names the GitHub issue a task works on (`owner/name#N`, its URL, or `#N` for the
repository's origin) and `take_over` takes that issue from its holder; a task's `issue` replaces
the spec's, and `take_over` only turns on. Before any task starts the batch refuses two tasks
that name the same issue, naming both, and takes every task's lease (run `<batch id>/<task id>`,
branch `hrn/<task id>`, and the task's or spec's `backend` only when one is set, since routing
picks an unset one later); if one is held, it gives back those it took and starts nothing. Each
task gives its issue back when it ends, is canceled, or the batch cannot save its record; lease
notes print as `[task] …` lines (see
[Issue leases](workspaces.md#issue-leases)).

Each task may also set `purpose`: `review`, `debug`, `implement`, `refactor`,
`test`, `research`, `plan` or `ops`. It is a task field, not a spec-wide default.
An invalid value is refused before any task starts. If omitted or empty, a valid
`Purpose: <category>` header on the first non-blank prompt line supplies it (see
[Declared purpose](commands.md#declared-purpose)). The effective declaration is
saved on the batch task result and each attempt's `agent.Task`, without changing
the prompt.

When writing implementation prompts for this repository, include the comment rule in
one line: "Comments say why, not what: one line, three at most; no issue numbers,
dates or review history in code."

entries.key: docs/batches.md > Batches and worktree cleanup > Batches (part 2)
entries.content:
each attempt's `agent.Task`, without changing the prompt. When writing implementation prompts for this repository, include the comment rule in one line: "Comments say why, not what: one line, three at most; no issue numbers, dates or review history in code."

For each task hrn creates branch `hrn/<id>` from the current `HEAD` (uncommitted changes
in the main worktree are not included) and gives it a worktree (see below), runs the
agent there, then the gates in order, stopping at the first non-zero exit or after 15
minutes. Whatever the agent left is committed on the branch as `<id>: <prompt>`, pass or
fail, so the work is on the branch whatever happens to the worktree; if that commit fails
(no git identity, a pre-commit hook) the task ends as `error` and the work stays
uncommitted in the worktree. An agent that commits its own work on the branch and leaves nothing
uncommitted gets no extra commit; the task records the branch's tip, so `diff` and merge see its
work. hrn reads the branch's tip and `HEAD` before and after the agent runs: when the agent
moved either itself (a commit of all or part of its work, a reset, a rename, a commit on another
branch or on none), the attempt records `agent_committed` and `hrn batch show` marks the task
`agent committed`. A tip that no longer contains the base (the agent reset or
rewrote the branch below it) is not recorded, since merging it would revert the base;
the attempt's error says so. Attempt notes appear beneath the task in `hrn batch` and
`hrn batch show`, and in MCP batch summaries as separate text lines and the optional
`notes` list on each task, including notes from earlier attempts and passing tasks.
Work the agent left uncommitted after moving `HEAD` off the task's branch
(detached, or onto another branch) is not committed there. The same rule applies
when the agent leaves a clean tree with `HEAD` off the task's branch at a commit
different from that branch's tip: the task ends as `error` (`canceled` if the batch
was stopped), saying where `HEAD` was and naming the off-branch commit's short SHA.
There is no retry or continuation; the worktree and any slot holding it stay in place,
the recorded commit is unchanged, and merge refuses the task. The failed attempt and
its note also appear in `hrn flow`, including when its flow is rebuilt from the saved
batch record. An agent that returns to its branch, or leaves `HEAD` at the task
branch's tip without uncommitted work, behaves as before. hrn writes `.hrn/.gitignore`
so the worktrees never show up
in the repository's status.

entries.key: docs/batches.md > Batches and worktree cleanup > Batches > Slots or fresh worktrees
entries.content:
### Slots or fresh worktrees

By default (`"worktrees": "slots"`) a task runs in one of the repository's reusable
[slots](workspaces.md), `<main checkout>/.hrn/slots/<n>`, so a `target/` or
`node_modules/` built by an earlier task is still there and the gates build only what
changed. Each running task leases a slot of its own, holding it with a lease that names
the hrn process. Its slot bound is `max(parallel, 5)`, capped at 10, counting
running tasks' and kept slots (below) together. It tries the slot
numbers from 1 that hold that many slots other than sessions' (`hrn ws take`,
a lease without a pid, held until `hrn ws free`), worked out again at every
try: with a five-slot bound, a session on slot 2 makes it try 1 and 3 to 6,
one on slot 10 changes nothing, and a session that takes a slot in the range
just as a task tries it widens the range at once (up to three times in a row;
a fourth session arriving in that instant fails the task rather than retrying
for ever). The range never passes slot 10; when no slot through 10 can be used,
the task waits or fails with the repository limit named. So a batch never
waits on a session, and its own slots stay bounded whatever the sessions do.
The task's branch is
made from the batch's base and checked out in the slot. When the task ends, pass, fail or
error, the slot is detached at the base and given back. Its ignored files stay for the
next task, and the work stays on branch `hrn/<id>`, which `diff`, `merge` and `rm` read.
An agent that ends on an empty orphan branch has no commits to keep; its slot is
detached at the base and given back too.
A failed task's line reads `branch hrn/<id> kept` rather than naming a folder, and the
record names the slot each task ran in (`worktree` and `slot`).

When every slot it tries is taken by another batch, or by this batch's own running
tasks once it holds as many as it may, a task does not fail:
it says it is waiting and which slots are held, looks again every 5 seconds, and is
canceled with the batch. A lease it cannot read keeps it waiting too, since one being
written reads on the next look. When such leases are all it is waiting for and every one has
stayed unreadable for 30 seconds (an empty or broken lease file, or a `<n>.lease.takeover`
file a crash left), no process will free them, so the task fails as `error` naming each file.
Check the slots with `hrn ws list`. A lease that stays unreadable, or a left `.takeover` file,
may be removed only while no hrn command at all runs on this repository, no `hrn ws` and no
`hrn batch`. A live take creates its lease empty and writes it next, before anything works in
the slot, so removing an empty lease lets a second take have the slot while the first goes on.
A live `hrn ws free` or takeover holds the `.takeover` file while the lease it guards may name
a dead process, and removing it lets another take in, whose fresh lease the free then removes.
Check with Task Manager or `tasklist | findstr hrn` on Windows, `pgrep hrn` elsewhere. When none can come free, because the rest are sessions', skipped
for what is in them or kept by this batch's own tasks (below), it fails as `error` instead. A slot that still holds files when its task ends (the commit
failed, or the agent left them off the task's branch), or an agent commit off the task's
branch (detached or on another branch, at a different tip), is not
given back: the task's error says `slot <n> kept` and why. Its lease
goes stale once hrn exits. Later takes still skip uncommitted work or a commit on no
remote, branch or tag; a clean slot whose commit is on the agent's other branch may
then be reused, with the commit still on that branch. To keep its work and free it,
see [A slot a batch kept](workspaces.md#a-slot-a-batch-kept).

`"worktrees": "fresh"` keeps the older behaviour, for a build from nothing: each task gets
a new worktree `.hrn/worktrees/<id>`, kept after the batch until `hrn batch rm`. Any other
value is refused before anything runs. `hrn eval` uses fresh worktrees unless its spec
says otherwise, because its judge reads each cell's worktree after the batch; it refuses
`slots` together with a judge.

entries.key: docs/batches.md > Batches and worktree cleanup > Batches > Slots or fresh worktrees (part 2)
entries.content:
batch until `hrn batch rm`. Any other value is refused before anything runs. `hrn eval` uses fresh worktrees unless its spec says otherwise, because its judge reads each cell's worktree after the batch; it refuses `slots` together with a judge.

A task can also set `expect`, a regular expression (Go RE2) its final answer must match.
It is checked before the gates and reported as one, `expect /pattern/`, so a task whose
answer is the deliverable can fail on what it said: `"expect": "(?i)^no\\b"` for "is
there a race here? answer yes or no". A retry after a miss is shown the answer it gave.

Gates run in the worktree the agent just edited, so an agent can make them pass by
weakening the tests. `protect` names the files the gates rely on, as globs relative to
the repository in which `**` stands for any number of folders:
`"protect": ["**/*_test.go", "scripts/check.sh"]`. After an attempt's run ends `ok`, hrn
compares those files with the batch's base, committed or not; a file the agent added is
not a change, a modified or removed one is. The attempt's record lists them under
`protected` and the batch shows `! protected files changed: ...`. `protect_mode` says what
that means: `report` (the default) keeps the verdict, `fail` fails the attempt before its
gates run, as a gate named `protect ...` whose output lists the files, so a retry is told
which ones to restore. A task's `protect` and `protect_mode` replace the spec's. Evals
default to `fail`.

Set `"retry_k": 3` on the spec or a task to try different brief additions after a
failed task. Values from 2 to 5 are accepted; a task value overrides the spec.
After the ordinary attempts fail, the task backend proposes additions, and each
candidate runs from the same base with the same gates and per-attempt budgets.
Candidates run concurrently and wait for available slots in slot mode. Passing
gates choose the winner: among passing candidates the fewest total input and
output tokens wins, with proposal order breaking equal-token ties. The batch
record keeps each addition, run ID, gate results, token total and winner flag.
If none passes the task stays failed; losing candidate branches and worktrees
are removed. Anything that cannot be removed stays claimed in the record (see
[run records](run-records.md)), so `hrn batch rm` and `hrn gc` can finish the
job. Evals refuse `retry_k`.

A failed attempt is retried on each backend named in `retry`, in order. The same name
may repeat, and `"retry": ["claude"]` after `"backend": "claude"` is the common case: a
second try with the same model, told what went wrong. A retry on a backend other than
the first attempt's drops the model and effort named or routed for that first backend,
and its record carries no `routed_by`. How the retry starts depends on how the attempt
failed.

With retrieval enabled, a same-scope retry after a failed gate searches again using
bounded failure evidence and the first attempt's pinned knowledge version. A change
of backend, model or retrieval scope is refused rather than silently repinned: a spec
or task with retrieval on whose `retry` names a backend other than the task's is refused
when the batch starts. When an attempt reaches its usage limit, or the first attempt or a
retry would move to the partner because the backend's limit is remembered, the task ends
there (status `fail`, its error saying the switch to the partner was skipped because
retrieval is bound to the task's backend) and nothing runs on the partner. A retry after required
retrieval failed before anything was pinned (the control service was unreachable, say)
searches afresh; once a pin is recorded, every retry honours it.

| Previous attempt | Next attempt |
|---|---|
| ran to the end, a gate failed | continues in the same worktree, on top of the work already committed, with the failing gate command, its exit code and output appended to the prompt |
| stopped at its plan's usage limit | continues in the same worktree, told that the limit stopped it and shown its last message |
| failed, refused or was cut short | starts afresh from the base commit (a new worktree, or the same slot with its branch reset to the base; the earlier attempt's commit leaves the branch, as a removed worktree's branch did; git's reflog still has it for a while), with one line saying how the previous attempt ended |

Backend preferences apply to both the spec's and each task's `backend` and `retry`.
A disabled primary backend is refused. Retry filtering preserves order and repeated
names, removes disabled entries, and refuses a nonempty list that becomes empty.
An explicit empty task retry list still overrides the spec's retries. See
[Backend preferences](backends.md#choosing-which-backends-hrn-may-use).

entries.key: docs/batches.md > Batches and worktree cleanup > Batches > Slots or fresh worktrees (part 3)
entries.content:
and `retry`. A disabled primary backend is refused. Retry filtering preserves order and repeated names, removes disabled entries, and refuses a nonempty list that becomes empty. An explicit empty task retry list still overrides the spec's retries. See [Backend preferences](backends.md#choosing-which-backends-hrn-may-use).

An attempt that ends `limited` is carried on by its ready enabled partner first, as
an extra attempt that does not use up a `retry` entry, and an attempt meant for a backend
whose limit is remembered starts on that partner (see [When a plan's usage limit is
reached](backends.md#when-a-plans-usage-limit-is-reached)). When both are limited, the attempt is
skipped, and a task with nothing left to run fails without starting an agent, its error
saying why. `no_switch` turns this off.

A continued attempt commits as `<id>: <prompt> (attempt N)`, so the branch reads as a
sequence of fixes. Each attempt records the prompt it was actually sent, whether it
continued, and `switched_from`, the backend a usage limit moved it from, which `hrn batch
--json` prints.

`hrn batch` refuses to start when tracked files in the repository are modified: every
worktree branches from `HEAD`, so that work would not reach the agents and the batch
would quietly be testing something else. Commit or stash first, or pass `--allow-dirty`
(spec field `allow_dirty`). Untracked files are not counted.

Nothing can answer approval prompts in a batch, so `mode` defaults to `auto` (file edits
allowed, no commands). Use `yolo` when the agent must build or run tests itself; the
gates run either way. Backend names, gate commands, durations and task budgets are all
checked before anything runs.

The [run budgets](commands.md#budgets) are spec fields too (`timeout`, `max_cost_usd`, `task_budget`), and
they apply per attempt rather than per task, so a retry gets its own allowance. A task
may set its own value or change the spec's, but zero means inherit, so it cannot remove
a limit the spec set.

Each attempt gives its agent and gates a temporary folder under `.hrn-gate-tmp` outside
the main checkout and any enclosing Git worktree. This keeps fixture discovery out of
the checkout and avoids cross-volume renames. If that folder cannot be created on the
worktree's volume, it uses the system temporary directory instead. It also falls back
if the parent is a symlink or, on Unix, permits access by other users. The attempt
removes its folder when it ends: `TMP`, `TEMP` and `TMPDIR` point there. `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` is `0` unless the
environment already sets it, or the worktree sets `incremental` under `[profile.dev]`
or `[profile.test]` (or one of their sub-tables) in `Cargo.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`,
or `.cargo/config`, or under `[build]` in either Cargo config file. Inline tables, dotted
keys and quoted table names are not read. A gate command may set its own values.

Each gate command gets 15 minutes before it is killed with its whole process tree;
`gate_timeout` (e.g. `"90s"`, `"45m"`, at most `24h`) changes that on the spec or on one
task, so a slow integration suite and a quick lint can share a batch. A killed gate fails
with `[timed out after …]` in its output, and its record says why it was killed (`killed`,
`"timeout"` with the `timeout` that applied, or `"canceled"` when the batch was
interrupted, even one that could not start because of it), so every report of it says
`killed after 15m0s (gate_timeout; set "gate_timeout" in the spec to allow more)` or
`canceled` rather than `exited -1`. The watch page's badge keeps that short (`killed ·
gate_timeout 15m0s`, the full text as its tooltip), and a retry is told the gate `was
killed after 15m0s by gate_timeout` without the advice, which is the operator's, so it
does not search the output for a failing test.

If the gate shell cannot start, the task fails with an infrastructure reason and
does not use any remaining `retry` backends. This covers a process start error
(including a missing shell interpreter), a shell that started but could not be waited
for (recorded as a wait failure, not a start failure), or a nonzero exit whose output was decoded
from UTF-16 and contains an `HCS_E_*` error code or `The Windows Subsystem for Linux`
launcher diagnostic within the first 1 KiB of decoded output.
The gate records the reason in `infrastructure_error`; the agent's work is still
committed for inspection. Other nonzero exits, including a command not found
inside a running shell, keep the normal retry behavior. Cancellation and
`gate_timeout` keep the behavior described above.

entries.content:
The gate records the reason in `infrastructure_error`; the agent's work is still committed for inspection. Other nonzero exits, including a command not found inside a running shell, keep the normal retry behavior. Cancellation and `gate_timeout` keep the behavior described above.

Gate output is decoded from UTF-16 to UTF-8 before it is checked, shortened,
recorded or shown. A little- or big-endian BOM identifies UTF-16; without a BOM,
alternating NUL bytes over the first few code units identify the byte order. One
mixed shape is split, since stdout and stderr can differ in encoding: UTF-16 (with a
BOM or detected as above) ending on a UTF-16 newline, then UTF-8 to the end with no
NUL or other control bytes than tab, newline, carriage return and escape. The split is
made only when the UTF-16 part decodes cleanly and the UTF-8 part does not also read
as clean UTF-16 text in one script, as a short final UTF-16 line in Cyrillic, CJK or
Gurmukhi can; such output is decoded as UTF-16 whole. Output too long to keep whole is
decoded on each side of its `[... N bytes truncated ...]` marker: the head loses a
character the cut ended inside, and the tail is read from the code-unit boundary that
`N` gives (dropping half of a surrogate pair the cut split), or as UTF-8 from its first
whole character, whichever decodes cleanly.

The record goes to `~/.hrn/batches/<id>.json`, written before the first task starts,
again each time a task moves on (an attempt's run starts or ends, a gate finishes, a task
ends) and at the end, so `hrn watch` and `hrn batch show` can follow it; `--json` prints
it, `-v` streams every agent's tool calls. Its `ownership` is 1 in records hrn writes now: a
fresh task owns its worktree and branch only when its `branch_made` says so (older records
lack the field and still load). Ctrl+C
cancels running agents and skips the rest. Exit status is 1 unless every task passed.
